A 45-year-old man presents to the clinic with acute back pain that began two days ago after lifting a
heavy box. He was initially evaluated in the emergency department, where imaging studies were
negative. He has no prior history of back pain or significant medical history. The pain does not radiate,
and a review of systems is unremarkable. Physical examination reveals tenderness and warmth over
the lumbar region, with exquisite tenderness of the soft tissue around L3. Applying anterior pressure to
the right transverse process reveals a woody end-feel that resolves with flexion at that level. The
patient is positioned for direct, passive treatment by lying lateral recumbent on the opposite side of the
posterior transverse process, but the motion barrier is challenging to localize. Which adjustment during
the setup would best isolate the dysfunction? Answer Choices: (A) Rotate the torso away from the
posterior transverse process (B) Pull the left upper extremity toward the table while side-bending the
torso (C) Rotate the torso toward the posterior transverse process (D) Flex the hips and knees to 90
degrees (E) Extend the lower extremities to increase lumbar lordosis (F) Pull the left upper extremity
inferiorly (G) Pull the right upper extremity anteriorly while rotating the torso (H) Pull the left upper
extremity out, twisting torso toward ceiling (I) Pull the right upper extremity superiorly (J) Pull the right

upper extremity out, twisting torso toward table
 A. Rotate the torso toward the posterior transverse process
B. Pull the right upper extremity out, twisting torso toward table
C. Pull the right upper extremity superiorly
D. Rotate the torso away from the posterior transverse process
E. Pull the left upper extremity out, twisting torso toward ceiling
F. Extend the lower extremities to increase lumbar lordosis
G. Pull the left upper extremity inferiorly
H. Pull the left upper extremity toward the table while side-bending the torso
I. Pull the right upper extremity anteriorly while rotating the torso
J. Flex the hips and knees to 90 degrees
